en: Itivuttaka 108 Catukkanipāta Brāhmaṇadhammayāgavagga Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having thus spoken, the Fortunate One further said this: “Brahmins, there are these four kinds of sacrifices. What four? The sacrifice of material goods, the sacrifice of the Dhamma, the sacrifice of fire, and the sacrifice of the self. These, Brahmins, are the four kinds of sacrifices. Of these four kinds of sacrifices, the sacrifice of the Dhamma is declared to be supreme. Thus spoke the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer, the Teacher, further said this: “The sacrifice of the Dhamma is the best among sacrifices; The Dhamma is the sweetest of all tastes; Truth is the best among things that lead out; And Nirvana is the highest of all states. This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, those brahmins rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Then a certain brahmin approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him. When they had concluded their polite conversation and cordial greetings, he sat down to one side. As he was sitting there, the Blessed One said to him: “Brahmin, there are these four kinds of gifts. What four? The gift of material goods, the gift of the Dhamma, the gift of fearlessness, and the gift of the Dhamma. These, brahmin, are the four kinds of gifts. Of these four kinds of gifts, the gift of the Dhamma is declared to be supreme. Thus spoke the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer, the Teacher, further said this: “The gift of the Dhamma is the best among gifts; The Dhamma is the sweetest of all tastes; Truth is the best among things that lead out; And Nirvana is the highest of all states. This is what the Blessed One said. Elated, that brahmin rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One. Thus have I heard. Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard:
"Bhikkhus, whatever bhikkhus are deceitful, stubborn, talkative, arrogant, insolent, and unconcentrated—those bhikkhus, bhikkhus, are not my followers."
“Monks, those monks have departed from this Dhamma and Vinaya; they do not attain growth, increase, or maturity in this Dhamma and Vinaya.
But those monks, monks, who are free from guile, free from chatter, wise, undeluded, and well-composed—they, monks, are my monks.
They have not departed from this Dhamma and Vinaya; they do attain growth, increase, and maturity in this Dhamma and Vinaya.”
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
Those who are haughty and unconcentrated do not grow in the Dhamma taught by the Perfectly Enlightened One.
Those who are unassuming, free from flattery, wise,
it is they indeed who cause the Dhamma to grow.
This meaning was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
